nodes.summary: If $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ are lex-minimal extensions, then their componentwise sum $\eta_1 + \eta_2$ is a lex-minimal extension.
nodes.title: Lex-minimal extensions are closed under addition

nodes.summary: Let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be a lex-minimal extension and let $p \ge 1$. If $e_{i+p} = e_i$ for every $i \ge 2$, then $e_{1+p} = e_1$, so the whole sequence $\eta$ is periodic with period $p$.
nodes.title: A lex-minimal extension periodic from its second entry is periodic

nodes.summary: Every lex-minimal extension satisfies the Average Condition.
nodes.title: Lex-minimal extensions satisfy the Average Condition

nodes.summary: For every natural number $c$, the constant sequence $(c, c, c, \dots)$ satisfies the Average Condition.
nodes.title: Constant sequences satisfy the Average Condition

nodes.summary: A sequence $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ of nonnegative integers satisfies the Average Condition when its upper average $A_0(\eta)$, the limit superior as $n \to \infty$ of the averages $A_{n,0}(\eta) = (e_1 + \dots + e_n)/n$ taken in the extended real line, equals $A_{i,0}(\eta)$ for some $i \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The Average Condition

nodes.summary: For every natural number $c$ and every $i \ge 1$, the average $A_{i,0}$ of the first $i$ entries of the constant sequence $(c, c, c, \dots)$ equals $c$.
nodes.title: Averages of a constant sequence

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 0$ and let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be the lex-minimal extension of its first $m$ entries, with averages $A_i = (e_1 + \dots + e_i)/i$ for $i \ge 1$. If $1 \le j \le m$ and $A_j = \max \{A_i \mid 1 \le i \le m\}$, then $A_i \le A_j$ for every $i \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The largest of the first $m$ averages is the largest average

nodes.summary: For every sequence $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ of nonnegative integers, the initial average $A_{1,0}(\eta)$ of its first entry equals $e_1$.
nodes.title: The first average is the first entry

nodes.summary: Let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be a binomid index, write $s_n = e_1 + \dots + e_n$, and for $i \ge 1$ and $l \ge 0$ let $A_{i,l} = (s_{i+l} - s_l)/i$ be the average of $e_{l+1}, \dots, e_{l+i}$. Then for all $i, l \ge 1$: $A_{i,l} \ge A_{i,0}$; $A_{ki,0} \ge A_{i,0}$ for every $k \ge 1$; and $A_{i+l,0} = \frac{i}{i+l} A_{i,l} + \frac{l}{l+i} A_{l,0}$.
nodes.title: Averages of a binomid index

nodes.summary: For a sequence $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ of nonnegative integers and $i \ge 1$, the average $A_{i,0}(\eta)$ is the rational number $s_i / i$, where $s_i = e_1 + \dots + e_i$ is the sum of the first $i$ entries; for $i = 0$ the value is $A_{0,0}(\eta) = 0$.
nodes.title: Initial averages of a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be the set of lex-minimal extensions, and for a natural number $l$ let $\sigma^l$ be the right shift that prepends $l$ zeros to a sequence. For natural numbers $l \neq m$, $\sigma^l(L) \cap \sigma^m(L) = \{(0, 0, 0, \dots)\}$: the only sequence in both images is the zero sequence.
nodes.title: Distinct shifts of lex-minimal extensions meet only in zero

nodes.summary: For every sequence $\eta$ of nonnegative integers, $\sigma^0(\eta) = \eta$, where $\sigma^l$ is the right shift that prepends $l$ zeros.
nodes.title: Shifting by zero places is the identity

nodes.summary: For a natural number $l$, the right shift $\sigma^l$ sends a sequence $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ of nonnegative integers to the sequence $(0, \dots, 0, e_1, e_2, \dots)$ obtained by prepending $l$ zeros: its first $l$ entries are $0$ and its $(l + i)$-th entry is $e_i$ for every $i \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Right shift of a sequence

nodes.summary: For every natural number $c$, the upper average $A_0$ of the constant sequence $(c, c, c, \dots)$ equals $c$.
nodes.title: Upper average of a constant sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\eta$ be a binomid index, let $s_i$ be the sum of its first $i$ entries, let $A_{i,0}(\eta) = s_i / i$ for $i \ge 1$, and let $A_0(\eta) = \limsup_{i \to \infty} A_{i,0}(\eta)$ be its upper average. Then, in the extended real numbers, $A_0(\eta) = \sup_{i \ge 1} A_{i,0}(\eta)$.
nodes.title: The upper average of a binomid index is the supremum of its averages

nodes.summary: For a sequence $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ of nonnegative integers with partial sums $s_i = e_1 + \dots + e_i$ and averages $A_{i,0}(\eta) = s_i / i$, the upper average of $\eta$ is $A_0(\eta) = \limsup_{i \to \infty} A_{i,0}(\eta)$, taken in the extended real numbers; it is $+\infty$ when $s_i / i$ is unbounded.
nodes.title: Upper average of a sequence

nodes.summary: For $k \ge 0$ let $L_k$ be the set of sequences of nonnegative integers that are the lex-minimal extension of their first $k$ entries, and let $\langle L_k \rangle$ be the submonoid of $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (under componentwise addition) generated by $L_k$. Then there are $n \ge 0$, a surjective monoid homomorphism $f \colon \mathbb{N}^n \to \langle L_k \rangle$ and a finite set $R$ of pairs of elements of…
nodes.title: Spans of lex-minimal extensions of a fixed length are finitely presented

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$, let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be the lex-minimal extension of its first $m$ entries, and write $S_i = e_1 + \dots + e_i$. Then for every $c \ge 1$ there are nonnegative integers $n_1, \dots, n_m$ with $\sum_{i=1}^m n_i i = c$ and $S_c = \sum_{i=1}^m n_i S_i$ that solve the unbounded knapsack problem with values $S_i$, weights $i$ and capacity $c$: all nonnegative integers $n'_1, \dots, n'_m$ with…
nodes.title: Partial sums of a lex-minimal extension solve a knapsack problem

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$, let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be the lex-minimal extension of its first $m$ entries, and let $p$ be a prime. Write $f_i = p^{e_i}$ for $i \ge 1$ and, for $1 \le k \le n$, let $[n, k]_f = \frac{f_n f_{n-1} \cdots f_{n-k+1}}{f_k f_{k-1} \cdots f_1}$ be the $f$-nomid coefficient, the generalized binomial coefficient of $f$. Then for every $n > m$ there is some $k$ with $1 \le k < n$ and $[n, k]_f = 1$.
nodes.title: Lex-minimal extensions have a nomid coefficient equal to one

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be the lex-minimal extension of its first $k$ entries, and write $S_i = e_1 + \dots + e_i$. Then for every $l$ there is a map $\pi \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $1 \le \pi(i) < i$ and $S_i = S_{\pi(i)} + S_{i - \pi(i)}$ for every $i$ with $k < i \le l$.
nodes.title: Late partial sums of a lex-minimal extension split

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 0$, let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be the lex-minimal extension of its first $m$ entries, with averages $A_i = (e_1 + \dots + e_i)/i$, and let $1 \le k \le m$ with $A_k = \max \{A_i \mid 1 \le i \le m\}$. Then $\eta$ is periodic after position $N = k m (m + 1)/2$: there is $p \ge 1$ with $e_{i+p} = e_i$ for all $i > N$.
nodes.title: A preperiod bound for lex-minimal extensions

nodes.summary: For $k \ge 0$ let $L_k$ be the set of sequences of nonnegative integers that are the lex-minimal extension of their first $k$ entries. Then the submonoid of $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (under componentwise addition) generated by $L_k$ is finitely generated, and only finitely many elements of $L_k$ are atomic binomid indices, that is, nonzero binomid indices that are not the sum of two nonzero binomid indices.
nodes.title: Spans of lex-minimal extensions of a fixed length are finitely generated

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$, let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be the lex-minimal extension of its first $m$ entries, with averages $A_i = (e_1 + \dots + e_i)/i$, and let $g$ be the greatest common divisor of the indices $1 \le i \le m$ with $A_i = \max \{A_j \mid 1 \le j \le m\}$. If $p$ is the least $q \ge 1$ such that $e_{i+q} = e_i$ for all sufficiently large $i$, then $g$ divides $p$.
nodes.title: The gcd of the maximizing indices divides the minimal period

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 0$, let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be the lex-minimal extension of its first $m$ entries, with averages $A_i = (e_1 + \dots + e_i)/i$, let $J$ be the set of indices $1 \le j \le m$ with $A_j = \max \{A_{j'} \mid 1 \le j' \le m\}$, and let $g = \gcd J$. Then $g$ divides every $i \ge 1$ such that $A_i = A_j$ for some $j \in J$.
nodes.title: Every index with maximal average is a multiple of the gcd of those up to $m$

nodes.summary: For $k \ge 0$ let $L_k$ be the set of sequences of nonnegative integers that are the lex-minimal extension of their first $k$ entries, let $\langle L_k \rangle$ be the submonoid of $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (under componentwise addition) generated by $L_k$, and let $\mathcal{A}_k$ be the set of elements of $L_k$ that are atomic binomid indices, that is, nonzero binomid indices that are not the sum of two nonzero…
nodes.title: The monoid of lex-minimal extensions is a directed union

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ there are infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that $p$ divides the binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$ for every $k$ with $1 \le k < n$.
nodes.title: Primes divide all inner binomial coefficients of infinitely many rows

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ be the Fibonacci numbers and $F_n! = F_1 F_2 \cdots F_n$ the Fibonacci factorial. For every prime $p$ there are infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that for every $k$ with $1 \le k < n$ the Fibonomial coefficient $F_n! / (F_k! \, F_{n-k}!)$ is an integer multiple of $p$.
nodes.title: Primes divide all inner Fibonomial coefficients of infinitely many rows

nodes.summary: Let $\mu = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be a binomid index such that for no $m$ is $\mu$ the lex-minimal extension of its first $m$ entries, and let $p$ be a prime. Write $f_i = p^{e_i}$ for $i \ge 1$ and let $[n, k]_f = \frac{f_n f_{n-1} \cdots f_{n-k+1}}{f_k f_{k-1} \cdots f_1}$ be the $f$-nomid coefficient. Then there are infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that for every $k$ with $1 \le k < n$ the coefficient…
nodes.title: Nomid coefficients of binomid indices that are not lex-minimal extensions

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 0$ and let $L_k$ be the set of sequences $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ of nonnegative integers that are the lex-minimal extension of $(e_1, \dots, e_k)$. A set $B$ of sequences of nonnegative integers is a basis of the submonoid generated by $L_k$ under componentwise addition if and only if $B$ is the set of nonzero atomic binomid indices that belong to $L_k$. Hence that set is the unique basis of this…
nodes.title: Basis of the span of the lex-minimal extensions of length $k$

nodes.summary: In every additive commutative monoid, the empty set is a basis of the subset $\{0\}$.
nodes.title: The empty set is a basis of the zero submonoid

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ be a type and let $M$ be a submonoid of $\mathbb{N}^\iota$ under componentwise addition. Let $A$ be the set of atoms of $M$: the elements $a \in M$ with $a \ne 0$ such that $y = 0$ or $z = 0$ whenever $a = y + z$ with $y, z \in M$. If every element of $M$ is a finite sum of elements of $A$, then a set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}^\iota$ is a basis of $M$ if and only if $B = A$; that is, $A$ is the unique…
nodes.title: Atoms are the unique basis of an atom-generated submonoid

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be the set of lex-minimal extensions, viewed inside the sequences of nonnegative integers under componentwise addition. A set $B$ of sequences of nonnegative integers is a basis of $L$ if and only if $B$ is the set of nonzero atomic binomid indices that belong to $L$. Hence that set is the unique basis of $L$.
nodes.title: Basis of the monoid of lex-minimal extensions

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $B$ be subsets of an additive commutative monoid. Then $B$ is a basis of $M$ when $M$ is the submonoid $\langle B \rangle$ generated by $B$ and no element of $B$ is a nonnegative integer combination of elements of $B$ in which its own coefficient is $0$: for all pairwise distinct $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_n \in B$, all nonnegative integers $c_1, \dots, c_n$ and every $j$, if…
nodes.title: Basis of a submonoid

nodes.summary: The constant sequence $(1, 1, 1, \dots)$ is a nonzero atomic binomid index: it is a nonzero binomid index that is not the sum of two nonzero binomid indices.
nodes.title: The constant sequence $1$ is atomic

nodes.summary: A sequence $\eta$ of nonnegative integers is a nonzero atomic binomid index (an element of the paper's set $\mathrm{Atom}$) when $\eta$ is a nonzero binomid index that is not the sum of two nonzero binomid indices: whenever $\eta = \eta_1 + \eta_2$ termwise with $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ binomid indices, $\eta_1 = 0$ or $\eta_2 = 0$.
nodes.title: Atomic binomid index

nodes.summary: For every natural number $c$, the constant sequence $(c, c, c, \dots)$ is a binomid index.
nodes.title: Constant sequences are binomid indices

nodes.summary: Let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be a sequence of nonnegative integers with partial sums $s_n = e_1 + \dots + e_n$ (so $s_0 = 0$). Then $\eta$ is a binomid index if and only if $s_{n-k} + s_k \le s_n$ for all $k$ and $n$ with $1 \le k < n$. Moreover, for every $m$, if $\eta$ is the lex-minimal extension of its first $m$ entries, then for every $n > m$
nodes.title: Partial-sum characterization of binomid indices

nodes.summary: Every non-decreasing sequence $e_1 \le e_2 \le \cdots$ of nonnegative integers is an infinite binomid index.
nodes.title: Monotone sequences are binomid indices

nodes.summary: An infinite binomid index is a sequence $(e_1, e_2, \dots)$ of nonnegative integers such that $\sum_{i=n-k+1}^{n} e_i \ge \sum_{i=1}^{k} e_i$ for all $1 \le k \le n$.
nodes.title: Binomid index

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be the lex-minimal extension of $(e_1, \dots, e_m)$. For $1 \le i \le m$ let $A_i = (e_1 + \dots + e_i)/i$, and let $A_{\max}$ be the largest of $A_1, \dots, A_m$. Let $g$ be the greatest common divisor of the indices $1 \le i \le m$ with $A_i = A_{\max}$. Then $g$ is the minimal eventual period of $\eta$: $g \ge 1$, $e_{i+g} = e_i$ for all sufficiently large $i$,…
nodes.title: Minimal period of a lex-minimal extension

nodes.summary: If an infinite binomid index $e = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ satisfies the Average Condition, then $e$ is a lex-minimal extension, that is, the lex-minimal extension of $(e_1, \dots, e_m)$ for some $m \ge 0$, and $e$ is eventually periodic: there are $N$ and $p \ge 1$ such that $e_{n+p} = e_n$ for all $n \ge N$.
nodes.title: The Average Condition gives eventually periodic lex-minimal extensions

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be a sequence of nonnegative integers and write $S_i = e_1 + \dots + e_i$. Suppose $S_i + S_j \le S_{i+j}$ for all $i, j \ge 1$ with $i + j \le k$. Then $\eta$ is the lex-minimal extension of $(e_1, \dots, e_k)$ if and only if, for every $r > k$, $S_i + S_j \le S_r$ for all $i, j \ge 1$ with $i + j = r$, with equality for at least one such pair $(i, j)$.
nodes.title: Partial-sum criterion for lex-minimal extensions

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $f = (f_1, f_2, \dots)$ be a sequence of nonnegative integers whose first $m$ entries form a finite binomid index, that is, $\sum_{i=n-k+1}^{n} f_i \ge \sum_{i=1}^{k} f_i$ for all $1 \le k \le n \le m$. Suppose that for every $n > m$ the entry $f_n$ equals the maximum, over $1 \le k < n$, of the integers $\sum_{i=1}^{k} f_i - \sum_{i=n-k+1}^{n-1} f_i$. Then $f$ is the lex-minimal extension of…
nodes.title: The lex-minimal extension is computed greedily

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $e_1 \le e_2 \le \cdots \le e_m$ be nonnegative integers. Then the periodic sequence $(e_1, \dots, e_m, e_1, \dots, e_m, \dots)$ is the lex-minimal extension of $(e_1, \dots, e_m)$.
nodes.title: Monotone finite binomid indices extend periodically

nodes.summary: If an infinite binomid index $e = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ is periodic, that is, there is $p \ge 1$ with $e_{i+p} = e_i$ for all $i$, then $e$ is a lex-minimal extension: it is the lex-minimal extension of $(e_1, \dots, e_m)$ for some $m \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Periodic binomid indices are lex-minimal extensions

nodes.summary: For every $m \ge 0$, the zero sequence $(0, 0, \dots)$ is the lex-minimal extension of its first $m$ entries.
nodes.title: The zero sequence is lex-minimal

nodes.summary: Let $e = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be a sequence of nonnegative integers and $m \ge 0$. Then $e$ is the lex-minimal extension of $(e_1, \dots, e_m)$ when $e$ is an infinite binomid index and, for every infinite binomid index $g$ with $g_i = e_i$ for all $i \le m$, either $g = e$ or $e$ is lexicographically smaller than $g$: there is a $j$ with $e_i = g_i$ for all $i < j$ and $e_j < g_j$.
nodes.title: Lex-minimal extension

nodes.summary: A sequence $e = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ of nonnegative integers is a lex-minimal extension when, for some $m \ge 0$, it is the lex-minimal extension of $(e_1, \dots, e_m)$. The set of all lex-minimal extensions is denoted $L$.
nodes.title: Lex-minimal extensions

nodes.summary: Let $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ be a sequence of nonnegative integers and $A_i = (e_1 + \dots + e_i)/i$. For $m = 1$, the set of indices $1 \le i \le m$ at which $A_i$ is maximal among $A_1, \dots, A_m$ is $\{1\}$.
nodes.title: Maximal-average indices for $m = 1$

nodes.summary: For a sequence $\eta = (e_1, e_2, \dots)$ of nonnegative integers and $m \ge 0$, let $A_i = (e_1 + \dots + e_i)/i$ be the average of the first $i$ entries of $\eta$. The set of maximal-average indices of $\eta$ up to $m$ is the set of all $i$ with $1 \le i \le m$ such that $A_j \le A_i$ for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le m$; for $m \ge 1$ these are the $i$ with $1 \le i \le m$ and $A_i = A_{\max}$, where…
nodes.title: Indices of maximal average

nodes.summary: Let $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ be infinite binomid indices and let $k \ge 0$. If the termwise sum $\eta_1 + \eta_2$ is the lex-minimal extension of its first $k$ entries, then $\eta_1$ is the lex-minimal extension of its first $k$ entries and $\eta_2$ is the lex-minimal extension of its first $k$ entries.
nodes.title: Summands of a lex-minimal extension are lex-minimal

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an additive commutative monoid and let $M$ and $B$ be subsets of $\alpha$. If $B$ is a basis of $M$, then $0 \notin B$.
nodes.title: A monoid basis does not contain zero

can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
